readerTitle: Uber's 2017 crisis: when star performers get a pass
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Uber, 2017년 문화 위기) + 가상 적용 (소매 매장, 가정 수리 업체)
insight: 회사의 진짜 가치는 벽에 붙은 문장이 아니라 리더가 최고 성과자에게 눈감아 주는 행동이 정한다.
misconception: 문화 문제는 나쁜 사람 몇 명의 문제이고, 그들을 내보내거나 가치 문구를 다시 쓰면 해결된다.

sources.text: Susan Fowler, "Reflecting on one very, very strange year at Uber" (blog post, February 19, 2017)
Covington & Burling (Eric Holder) recommendations to Uber's board, released by Uber in June 2017
New York Times coverage of Travis Kalanick's resignation as Uber CEO (June 2017)
Dara Khosrowshahi, LinkedIn post on Uber's new cultural norms (November 2017)
Mike Isaac, Super Pumped: The Battle for Uber (2019), on Uber's original 14 values

factChecks.note: Fowler 블로그 게시일 2017년 2월 19일, 내용 요약(관리자 신고 후 HR이 '고성과자'이고 초범이라는 이유로 강한 조치를 하지 않았고, 이후 다른 여성들도 같은 관리자를 신고했다는 사실을 알게 됨)을 원문과 대조하세요. 카드에는 직접 인용 없이 요약만 썼습니다.
Perkins Coie 조사 후 '20명 이상 해고'(2017년 6월 초 보도)를 확인하세요. Holder 보고서 권고안 수는 47개로 널리 보도되었으나 카드에는 'dozens'로만 적었습니다.
Kalanick: 2017년 6월 중순 휴직 발표, 같은 달 투자자 압력 속에 CEO 사임. Khosrowshahi: 2017년 8월 말 CEO 선임, 11월 새 문화 규범('We do the right thing. Period.') 발표. 날짜를 보도자료로 재확인하세요.
원래 14개 가치 중 'Always be hustlin'', 'Toe-stepping'(Meritocracy and toe-stepping), 'Super pumped', 'Principled confrontation' 표기를 Isaac(2019) 또는 당시 보도로 확인하세요.
2017년 Uber에는 #DeleteUber, Waymo 소송 등 다른 악재도 겹쳤습니다. 7번 카드에서 결과를 문화 하나로만 설명하지 않도록 단서를 달았습니다.

cards.title: Uber's 2017 crisis: when star performers get a pass
body: In February 2017, a former Uber engineer named Susan Fowler published a blog post about her year at the company.

She described reporting her manager for harassment. According to her account, HR kept the punishment light, partly because he was seen as a high performer. Within months, Uber's founder was out as CEO.

image.label: A single blog post on a laptop rippling across a city of offices
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 노트북 화면의 블로그 글 한 편에서 파문이 퍼져 나가 주변 사무실 건물들을 흔드는 장면. 실제 Uber 로고, 앱 화면, 인물 얼굴은 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: You sit on Uber's board, February 2017.
body: The post is spreading fast. It describes not one bad manager but a pattern: complaints ignored, results excused. Uber is growing fast and raising huge sums.

options.text: Investigate the named manager, act on the findings, and apologize publicly
options.feedback: It handles the case quickly. But the post described a system that protected him, and that system would stay in place.

options.text: Order an outside review of complaints, values and leadership behavior across the company
options.feedback: Slower and riskier, because it may reach the top. It is also the only option that tests whether the problem is a person or the culture.

options.text: Let the CEO handle it internally so growth isn't distracted
options.feedback: It keeps the company focused, but it asks the system that failed to judge itself. Trust inside and outside drops further.

cards.title: The review reached the top.
body: Uber hired former US Attorney General Eric Holder's law firm for a broad review. A separate investigation looked at specific complaints, and more than 20 employees were fired.

In June 2017, Holder's team gave the board dozens of recommendations, including stronger HR, more board oversight and rewriting the company's values. Days later, CEO Travis Kalanick took leave. Under investor pressure, he resigned that same month.

cards.title: Culture is what you tolerate from your best people.
body: Uber had 14 written values, including *Always be hustlin'*, *Toe-stepping* and *Super pumped*. They praised aggression and winning, with no clear line on how.
Values are tested when a top performer crosses a line. **Whatever leaders excuse in that moment becomes the real value**, and every employee watching learns it faster than any poster.

image.label: A values poster on the wall, while a manager waves through a star employee
image.brief: 사무실 벽에 'Our values' 포스터가 걸려 있고, 그 앞에서 관리자가 트로피를 든 직원에게 손짓으로 '괜찮다'고 통과시키는 장면. 뒤에서 다른 직원들이 지켜봄. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: A new CEO rewrote the rules, then had to live them.
body: Dara Khosrowshahi became CEO in late August 2017. In November he replaced the 14 values with new cultural norms, led by **"We do the right thing. Period."**
The words mattered less than the signal around them: leaders replaced, people fired, the board changed. Employees believe new values only when they see someone powerful held to them.

cards.title: The same pattern in a store.
body: A regional retail chain has a store manager who beats every sales target. His staff turnover is the highest in the company, and exit interviews mention yelling.
Head office promotes him anyway. Within a year, other managers start copying his style. Nobody changed the values statement. Leadership simply showed what wins.

image.label: Store managers copying one manager's loud style across several shops
image.brief: 여러 매장이 나란히 있는 단면도. 한 매장의 관리자가 직원에게 소리치고 있고, 옆 매장들의 관리자들이 같은 자세를 따라 하기 시작함. 실제 소매 브랜드 로고 없음.

cards.title: Don't over-read one story.
body: Drive and ambition aren't toxic. The problem is ambition with no line, where results buy exceptions.

Rewriting values alone changes little. Uber's reset came with new leaders, firings and new processes. And 2017 also brought lawsuits and a boycott campaign, so not every outcome can be pinned on culture.

cards.title: Now it's a home repair company.
body: Your best electrician brings in the most repeat clients. He also belittles apprentices, and two have quit this year. The rest of the crew is watching what you do.

options.text: Keep him as is and move apprentices to other crews
options.feedback: You protect revenue this month. The crew learns that results buy a pass, and that lesson spreads.

options.text: Name the behavior, set a clear consequence, and follow through even if he leaves
options.feedback: You may lose a strong earner. You show everyone that the standard applies to stars too.

options.text: Give him a bonus tied to apprentice retention
options.feedback: It might change his behavior. It also suggests the standard is something you pay for, not something you hold.

cards.title: Your real values are the exceptions you make.
body: People learn culture by watching what happens when a star crosses a line.
**Try it today:** name your strongest performer. Write down one behavior you've let slide. Ask what you'd do if a new hire did the same.
